sentences.en: Off a busy street in Brooklyn, New York, sits a storefront called Monica's Hair Salon.
sentences.zh: 在纽约布鲁克林一条繁忙的街道旁，有一家名为莫妮卡美发沙龙的店面。

sentences.en: A salon our producer Priscilla Alabi visited a few weeks ago.
sentences.zh: 这是我们的制片人普iscilla Alabi几周前参观过的一家沙龙。

sentences.en: I've been going to hair salons like this since I was little.
sentences.zh: 我从小就一直去这种美发沙龙。

sentences.en: There are places where people come for their hair, but also for advice, gossip, celebrations.
sentences.zh: 这里人们不仅为了弄头发而来，还为了寻求建议、八卦和庆祝。

sentences.en: I just love us so much.
But to ask for a birthday hug.
sentences.zh: 而是来要一个生日抱抱的。

sentences.en: Well, this young lady, oh God, has been taking care of me since I was like 12.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这位年轻女士，天哪，自我大概12岁起就一直在照顾我。
这是洛林·塞缪尔的沙龙。

sentences.en: Today, she's about to give a customer a classic salon treatment.
sentences.zh: 今天，她准备给一位顾客做一个经典的美发护理。

sentences.en: One I've been thinking a lot about lately.
sentences.zh: 这个护理我最近一直在想。

sentences.en: What are you doing to your customer's hair right now?
sentences.zh: 你现在正在给顾客的头发做什么？

sentences.en: I was nine, maybe ten years old.
The first time a chemical relaxer touched my virgin hair.
sentences.zh: 当化学顺直剂第一次接触到我从未处理过的头发时。

sentences.en: That's the actual term for unprocessed hair.
sentences.zh: 这是指未经处理的头发的专业术语。

sentences.en: My natural kinky coils made hair grooming days very challenging.
sentences.zh: 我天然的卷曲发丝让打理头发的日子充满挑战。

sentences.en: So my mom and I decided to relax my hair to make it more manageable.
sentences.zh: 所以我妈妈和我决定做头发顺直，让它更好打理。

sentences.en: I was so excited for the possibility of long, flowy hair that a comb could easily pass through.
sentences.zh: 我当时超级兴奋，幻想着能拥有一头梳子一疏到底的长发、飘逸的秀发。

sentences.en: So what does it look like, the actual physical object itself?
sentences.zh: 那它看起来是什么样的，就那个实体本身而言？

sentences.en: Hmm, kind of like cream cheese, a little bit.
sentences.zh: 嗯，有点像奶油乳酪，有一点像。

sentences.en: It comes in a tub, like usually a plastic tub.
sentences.zh: 它装在一个罐子里，通常是塑料罐。

sentences.en: It kind of doesn't smell like anything.
sentences.zh: 它闻起来好像没什么气味。

sentences.en: But it probably burns the same way though, right?
sentences.zh: 不过它烧起来的感觉应该是一样的吧？

sentences.en: The first time I was preparing to get my hair relaxed, I was instructed very seriously,
sentences.zh: 我第一次准备去做头发顺直时，我被非常严肃地叮嘱过，

sentences.en: don't wash or scratch your scalp for at least one week before your appointment, because that
sentences.zh: 在预约前至少一周不要洗头或抓头皮，因为这

sentences.en: In previous salon visits, I'd seen women yowl when the pain got unbearable.
sentences.zh: 在之前去美发店的时候，我曾见过女人们因为疼痛难忍而发出号叫。

sentences.en: I didn't know it then, but I was being initiated into something much bigger than a hairstyle.
sentences.zh: 我当时并不知道，我正在被引入一种远比发型更宏大的事物中。

sentences.en: And it burns towards the end if you leave it in too long.
sentences.zh: 如果停留时间太久，到了尾声时它会灼痛。

sentences.en: So you're just supposed to end it to the hair shaft and then keep applying it to the creamy crack.
sentences.zh: 所以你只需要把它涂抹到发干上，然后继续涂抹在俗称“柔顺剂”的乳状直发剂上。

sentences.en: That's the relaxer's nickname, creamy crack, because it's said that relaxing your hair is addictive.
sentences.zh: 那是直发膏的外号，叫“乳状裂纹”，因为据说拉直头发是会成瘾的。

sentences.en: Once you start, it's very hard to stop.
sentences.zh: 一旦你开始，就很难停下来。

sentences.en: If you stop, the hair breaks off where the new curly growth meets the already straightened dead hair.
sentences.zh: 如果你停下来，头发会在新长出的卷发和已经拉直的死发交界处断裂。

sentences.en: Oh yeah, there's no resistance in that hair anymore with the comb.
sentences.zh: 哦，是的，梳子梳过那部分头发时已经完全没有阻力了。

sentences.en: The hair in the back where you started.
sentences.zh: 后脑勺你最开始弄的那部分头发。
你看到那撮难搞的头发了吗？

sentences.en: Today, somewhere between 85 and 95% of Black women in the United States have used a chemical relaxer
sentences.zh: 如今，在美国有大约85%到95%的黑人女性在一生中至少使用过一次化学直发剂

sentences.en: at least once in their lifetime, as I did starting at age 9 for years.
sentences.zh: 就像我一样，从9岁开始用了好多年。

sentences.en: Fast forward to 2023, while scrolling through Instagram, a targeted ad stopped me cold.
sentences.zh: 快进到2023年，当我在Instagram上刷动态时，一条精准投放的广告让我瞬间呆住了。

sentences.en: If you used chemical hair straightener and were later diagnosed with uterine fibroids,
sentences.zh: 如果你使用过化学美发直发剂，后来被诊断出患有子宫肌瘤，
请立即联系我们事务所。

sentences.en: A law firm wants me to join in a class action lawsuit.
sentences.zh: 一家律所想让我加入集体诉讼。

sentences.en: I had just been diagnosed with fibroids, a condition that disproportionately affects Black women.
sentences.zh: 我刚刚被诊断出患有子宫肌瘤，这是一种对黑人女性影响尤为严重的疾病。

sentences.en: The new research linking chemical hair relaxer to uterine fibroids may help explain this disparity.
sentences.zh: 将化学直发剂与子宫肌瘤联系起来的新研究，或许有助于解释这种差异。

sentences.en: There are many ads like this.
Did you or a loved one develop cancer after using hair relaxing or hair straightening products?
sentences.zh: 你或你爱的人在使用美发直发或顺发产品后患上癌症了吗？

sentences.en: If so, you may be able to sue the hair product manufacturer for damages.
sentences.zh: 如果是这样，你或许可以起诉美发产品制造商以获得赔偿。

sentences.en: Fibroids, uterine cancer, ovarian cancer, all implying that this thing so many Black women use,
sentences.zh: 肌瘤、子宫癌、卵巢癌，这一切都在暗示，这个无数黑人女性都在使用、

sentences.en: happening in so many salons across America and even the world, could actually be making us sick.
sentences.zh: 在全美乃至全世界无数美发沙龙里都在进行的东西，实际上可能正在让我们生病。

sentences.en: From 99% Invisible and BBC Studios, this is the history of the United States in 100 Objects.
sentences.zh: 本节目由《99%隐形》与BBC工作室联合制作，这里是“100件物品中的美国历史”。

sentences.en: Today, the chemical hair relaxer, a ubiquitous American product that built Black wealth and
sentences.zh: 今天的主题是化学直发剂，这是一种无处不在的美国产品，它创造了黑人财富并

sentences.en: But it also taught generations to see their hair as a problem to be solved.
sentences.zh: 但它也教育了几代人，让他们把自己的头发看作是一个需要解决的问题。

sentences.en: And now research is revealing a physical coSt.
sentences.zh: 而现在，研究正在揭示其肉体上的代价。

sentences.en: This is a story of how those two truths came to exist at the same time.
sentences.zh: 这是一个关于这两种真相如何同时存在的故事。

sentences.en: Producer Priscilla Alabi has the story.
sentences.zh: 制作人普莉希拉·阿拉比为您讲述这个故事。

sentences.en: When I saw the targeted ad soon after my fibroid diagnosis, I wanted answers.
sentences.zh: 当我刚确诊肌瘤不久看到那条定向广告时，我想要找寻答案。
我们是怎么走到这一步的？

sentences.en: Where so many Black women were doing this to ourselves.
sentences.zh: 为什么那么多黑人女性一直在对自己的身体做这种事。

sentences.en: Tharps and I am a journalist and the co-author of Hair Story,
sentences.zh: ·塔尔普斯，我是一名记者，也是《发的故事：

sentences.en: Untangling the Roots of Black Hair in America.
sentences.zh: 解开美国黑人发型之根》的合著者。

sentences.en: So I reached out to Lori Tharps, a journalist and hair historian who spent the last quarter
sentences.zh: 因此，我联系了洛里·塔尔普斯，她是一位记者兼发型史学家，在过去的四分之一

sentences.en: century asking similar questions about hair.
sentences.zh: 个世纪以来都在提出关于头发的类似问题。

sentences.en: So in your research, what surprised you most about the relationship Black Americans have
sentences.zh: 所以在你的研究中，美国黑人与他们
拉直头发的关系，最让你惊讶的是什么？

sentences.en: I think the thing that was the most interesting, and not in a good way, was how early the quest
sentences.zh: 我认为最有趣、而且并非好玩的是，早在沦为奴隶时期，

sentences.en: for straightening our hair began as enslaved individuals.
sentences.zh: 我们对拉直头发的追求就开始了。

sentences.en: And the fact that that yearning for straight hair as a source of assimilation is still with us.
sentences.zh: 而且这种对直发的渴望作为同化来源至今仍然伴随着我们。

sentences.en: But Lori says starting the story with enslavement is like starting at chapter two.
sentences.zh: 但洛里说，把这个故事从奴隶制开始讲起，就像是从第二章开始读。

sentences.en: You miss a lot of context.
And when you skip chapter one, Black people end up looking obsessed, even pathological, about their hair.
sentences.zh: 而当你跳过第一章时，黑人最终看起来就会对自己的头发有着痴迷，甚至病态。

sentences.en: If you go chapters before arrival, then we know that Black people have always been artistic
sentences.zh: 如果你追溯到到达之前的那些章节，我们就会知道黑人在发型设计上一直极具艺术感

sentences.en: There was a rich hairdressing tradition in Africa.
sentences.zh: 非洲有着丰富的发型设计传统。

sentences.en: That was a part of their culture.
sentences.zh: 那是他们文化的一部分。

sentences.en: Hairstyling was fundamental to showcasing and sharing your identity.
sentences.zh: 发型设计是展示和分享个人身份认同的基础。

sentences.en: You had a hairstyle that connected you to a tribe, to a family, to a people.
sentences.zh: 你拥有一个能将你与部落、家庭、民族联系起来的发型。
这是一种祖先留下的遗产。

sentences.en: So when Africans were enslaved and brought to America, their hairdressing traditions transformed.
sentences.zh: 因此，当非洲人被沦为奴隶并带到美洲时，他们的发型传统发生了转变。

sentences.en: What used to be a way to express yourself that connects you to your people and your identity
sentences.zh: 曾经那种表达自我、将你与族人和身份连接在一起的方式

sentences.en: suddenly became a strategy for survival.
sentences.zh: 突然变成了一种生存策略。

sentences.en: Black people were interested in straightening their hair very soon after being kidnapped and brought to the colonies
sentences.zh: 黑人在被绑架并带到殖民地后不久就开始对拉直头发感兴趣，

sentences.en: because they were told that their hair was inferior, that it was ugly, that it was more animalistic.
sentences.zh: 因为他们被告知他们的头发是低劣的、丑陋的、更具动物性的。

sentences.en: We simply wanted to stop being treated like animals.
sentences.zh: 我们只是想停止被当作动物对待。

sentences.en: And then hair straightening became a visual way to demonstrate our equality.
sentences.zh: 然后拉直头发成了一种展示我们平等的可视化方式。

sentences.en: They created new techniques and tools from what was available.
sentences.zh: 他们利用现有的东西创造了新技术和工具。

sentences.en: They had to get creative because they didn't have the tools or materials that they had in Africa.
sentences.zh: 他们必须发挥创造力，因为他们没有在非洲时的工具或材料。

sentences.en: So instead of something like palm oil that was very common in Africa to soften the hair, they would use butter.
sentences.zh: 因此，他们不用非洲非常普遍的用来软化头发的棕榈油之类的东西，而是用黄油。

sentences.en: They turned cornmeal and kerosene into shampoo, baking grease and butter into conditioner.
sentences.zh: 他们把玉米粉和煤油变成洗发水，把培根油和黄油变成护发素。

sentences.en: Butter knives became crude flat irons.
sentences.zh: 黄油刀变成了简陋的直发器。

sentences.en: They would wrap the hair in yarn to kind of pull the kinks out.
sentences.zh: 他们会用纱线包裹头发来把卷曲拉直。
非常具有发明性，非常具有创造性的方法。

sentences.en: They were so inventive that their techniques became legendary.
sentences.zh: 他们太有创造力了，以至于他们的技术成为了传奇。

sentences.en: So sought after that they became the barbers and wig makers of choice for white people.
sentences.zh: 如此抢手，以至于他们成了白人的首选理发师和假发制作师。

sentences.en: White people paid for their hands, their skill, their artistry.
sentences.zh: 白人为他们的双手、他们的技能、他们的艺术性付钱。

sentences.en: And that access to wealth, that became a pathway.
sentences.zh: 而对财富的接触，变成了一条途径。

sentences.en: They were able to make enough money, many of them, to buy themselves out of slavery.
sentences.zh: 他们中的许多人能够赚到足够的钱，来为自己赎身摆脱奴隶身份。

sentences.en: Many of the early Black universities and other Black institutions were actually funded or founded by Black barbers.
sentences.zh: 许多早期的黑人大学和其他黑人机构实际上都是由黑人理发师资助或创立的。

sentences.en: For example, they funded Wilberforce University, one of the first HBCUs owned and operated entirely by African-Americans, built in large part on the earnings from hairdressing.
sentences.zh: 例如，他们资助了威尔伯福斯大学，这是第一所完全由非裔美国人拥有和运营的历史悠久的黑人大学（HBCU），其建设在很大程度上依靠美发赚取的收入。

sentences.en: Now, interestingly, though, to be clear, the Black barbers at this time were not barbering other Black people's hair.
sentences.zh: 有趣的是，需要说明的是，当时的黑人理发师并不是为其他黑人理发。

sentences.en: They were barbering white people's hair, which is sadly ironic because they couldn't do their own.
sentences.zh: 他们是为白人理发，这听起来有些可悲的讽刺，因为他们不能为自己人理发。

sentences.en: I mean, maybe, you know, after hours, but they, you know, they couldn't have a barbershop where they did white clients and Black clients because that would never fly.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，也许你知道，在打烊之后，但你知道，他们不可能开一家既接待白人客户又接待黑人客户的理发店，因为那样根本行不通。

sentences.en: Black folks continue to innovate with their own hair, though.
sentences.zh: 不过，黑人群体一直在用自己的头发进行创新。

sentences.en: And by the early 1900s, that innovation would turn into full-fledged empires.
sentences.zh: 到了20世纪初，这种创新将演变成成熟的商业帝国。

sentences.en: Let's start with two women, Madam C.J.
sentences.zh: 让我们从两位女性开始，玛丽·阿瑟·莫罗·沃克（Madam C.J.）

sentences.en: Walker and Annie Turnbull Malone, the first pioneers in Black hair care as an industry.
sentences.zh: 沃克和安妮·特恩布尔·马隆，她们是黑人美发护理作为产业的第一批先驱。

sentences.en: They took the hodgepodge of hair straightening methods floating around and turned them into an actual system.
sentences.zh: 他们将当时流传的各种零散的头发直发方法整理成了一个真正的系统。
玛丽·阿瑟·莫罗·沃克（Madam C.J.）

sentences.en: Walker and Annie Turnbull Malone became very wealthy by selling the idea of straight hair, but not with chemicals.
sentences.zh: 沃克和安妮·特恩布尔·马隆通过出售直发的理念变得非常富有，但用的不是化学制剂。

sentences.en: They used hot combs and worked them through the hair with pomade to get a sleek, straight look.
sentences.zh: 他们使用热梳，并在发油的配合下将其梳过头发，以获得光滑、笔直的外观。

sentences.en: But more importantly, they built an entire industry and economy around Black hair care that didn't exist before.
sentences.zh: 但更重要的是，他们围绕黑人美发护理建立了一个以前并不存在的完整产业和经济。

sentences.en: You have to remember that during slavery, Black women were not given time to really pay attention to their hair in terms of, like, really taking care of it.
sentences.zh: 你必须记住，在奴隶制时期，黑人女性没有时间真正关注她们的头发，比如真正去护理它。
玛丽·阿瑟·莫罗·沃克（Madam C.J.）

sentences.en: Walker and Annie Turnbull Malone were both really good at creating a beauty culture around hair for Black women.
sentences.zh: 沃克和安妮·特恩布尔·马隆都非常善于为黑人女性创造一种围绕头发的美丽文化。

sentences.en: And so it would be like, we're going to wash your hair.
sentences.zh: 所以就像是，我们要洗你的头发。

sentences.en: We're going to massage your scalp.
We're going to straighten your hair.
sentences.zh: 我们要把你的头发弄直。

sentences.en: And in so doing, Madam C.J.
sentences.zh: 正因如此，玛丽·阿瑟·莫罗·沃克（Madam C.J.）

sentences.en: Walker became the first self-made millionaire woman in America, Black or white.
sentences.zh: 沃克成为了美国第一位靠自己白手起家的女性百万富翁，无论黑人还是白人。

sentences.en: But the issue with straightening your hair with a hot comb was that the results were temporary.
sentences.zh: 但是用热梳拉直头发的问题在于，效果是暂时的。

sentences.en: Because once moisture hit the hair, sweat, humidity, rain, it went back to its natural state.
sentences.zh: 因为一旦水分接触到头发，比如汗水、湿气、雨水，它就会恢复到自然状态。

sentences.en: But someone was about to find a permanent solution and completely by accident.
sentences.zh: 但有人将要找到一个永久的解决方案，而且完全是一个意外。

sentences.en: Garrett Augustus Morgan was a tailor in Cleveland, Ohio, in the early 1900s.
sentences.zh: 加勒特·奥古斯塔斯·摩根是20世纪初俄亥俄州克利夫兰的一名裁缝。
zh_words: 加勒特·奥古斯塔斯·摩根

sentences.en: He was trying to create a substance that would prevent high-speed machines and needles from destroying material like wool and other animal fur.
sentences.zh: 他当时正试图创造一种物质，可以防止高速机器和针具损坏羊毛和其他动物毛皮等材料。

sentences.en: One day, he tried a particular concoction and he noticed the thick texture of the fur relaxed.
sentences.zh: 有一天，他尝试了一种特定的混合物，并注意到毛皮厚实的质地变松弛了。

sentences.en: Next, he tries a solution on his neighbor's dog.
sentences.zh: 接着，他在邻居的狗身上尝试了一种溶液。

sentences.en: But the dog's fur comes out straight.
Morgan then tries a substance on his own hair next.
sentences.zh: 接下来，摩根在自己的头发上尝试了这种物质。

sentences.en: And his hair also becomes straight.
And it was like an accidental discovery.
sentences.zh: 这就像是一个意外的发现。

sentences.en: He accidentally discovered that if you mix lye and some other things, we could straighten the hair.
sentences.zh: 他偶然发现，如果你把碱液和其他一些东西混合在一起，我们就可以把头发拉直。

sentences.en: Lye, spelled L-Y-E, is sodium hydroxide.
sentences.zh: 碱液，拼写为L-Y-E，是氢氧化钠。

sentences.en: A caustic chemical that people already knew could straighten hair.
sentences.zh: 人们早就知道这是一种可以拉直头发的苛性化学品。

sentences.en: But it was too dangerous, too corrosive to use safely.
sentences.zh: 但它太危险、太具腐蚀性，无法安全使用。

sentences.en: What Morgan found was a formula that made it possible to use lye on human hair more safely.
sentences.zh: 摩根发现的配方，使得在人类头发上更安全地使用烧碱成为可能。

sentences.en: And it was men, not women, who first were willing to gamble with the new chemical straightener.
sentences.zh: 而且首先愿意拿这种新型化学直发剂冒险的是男人，而不是女人。

sentences.en: They wanted that sleek, processed look.
sentences.zh: 他们想要那种顺滑、加工过的造型。

sentences.en: And one of the most iconic lores about this conch look is one featuring the equally iconic Malcolm X,
sentences.zh: 关于这个康克头造型最标志性的传说之一，就涉及同样标志性的马尔科姆·X，

sentences.en: when he was a teenager, who had just moved to the big city of Boston.
sentences.zh: 在他十几岁的时候，他刚搬到波士顿这样的大城市。

sentences.en: And the story that he shares about how important it was for him to look cool,
